title: Saboojsathi 2026: Free Cycle for WB Students, Portal Login
meta_description: Saboojsathi 2026: free bicycles for Class 9-12 students in West Bengal. Portal login at wbsaboojsathi.gov.in, eligibility, distribution status and grievance.

hero.one_liner: How the Saboojsathi free bicycle scheme works for West Bengal students, who qualifies, how to log in at wbsaboojsathi.gov.in to check distribution status, and what to do if your cycle has not arrived.

what_is_it: Saboojsathi is a West Bengal government scheme that gives a free bicycle to every student in Class 9 to Class 12 in government, government-aided and recognised madrasah schools.
The name means Green Companion in Bengali. The idea is simple: a cycle removes the travel barrier that makes many students, especially girls in rural areas, drop out of school.
The scheme was launched in 2015 and has distributed over 1.2 crore bicycles since then. It is one of the state's best-known student welfare schemes.
You do not apply for it yourself. Your school adds eligible students to a list, so the most useful thing you can do is understand the process and check your distribution status online.
This guide covers exactly that: who gets a cycle, how to log in and check status, and what to do if your cycle has not reached you.
The aim throughout is to give you the official portal, the real eligibility rules and the exact steps, so you can confirm your own status without guesswork.
Saboojsathi has become a model that other states have looked at, precisely because a low-cost cycle solves a stubborn problem at scale.

extra_sections.heading: What Saboojsathi Gives and Who Runs It
content: Saboojsathi gives one free bicycle to each eligible student. There is no fee, no deposit and nothing to repay.
The scheme is run by the Department of Backward Classes Welfare, Government of West Bengal. A steering committee and district nodal officers handle distribution on the ground.
The bicycles are bought in bulk by the state through a tender process and handed over school by school. This is why distribution happens in batches rather than all at once.
For students, the practical takeaway is that the cycle comes through your school. Your job is to make sure your name is on the school's list and then track the distribution status.
If you also need housing help, see our Bangla Awas Yojana list guide.
The cycles themselves are sturdy, standard-model bicycles meant for daily school use. They are not premium cycles, but they are reliable and built to last several school years.
Because the cycle is meant for the student named on the list, it should not be sold or transferred. It is a personal benefit tied to your school enrolment.

extra_sections.heading: Saboojsathi Portal Login and Status Check
content: The official portal is wbsaboojsathi.gov.in. This is where you check your distribution status and raise complaints.
For the student login, you need your Applicant ID and your date of birth. The Applicant ID comes from your school.
If you do not have an Applicant ID, you do not log in directly. Instead you use the public Bicycle Distribution Record search, which needs your district, block, school and class.
Always use the official wbsaboojsathi.gov.in address. Avoid look-alike sites that ask for money, since the scheme is completely free.
Bookmark the portal once you reach it correctly. Searching afresh each time risks landing on a copycat site, and the genuine one always ends in gov.in.
Keep the page details handy if you are helping a younger sibling check their status. The same login and search method works for every eligible student.
The portal works on a basic phone browser, which matters since most families check on mobile. You do not need a computer to log in or run the distribution search.

extra_sections.heading: Checking the Distribution Record District Wise
content: The distribution record on the portal is organised district wise and school wise. This is how you confirm whether your school's batch has been delivered.
On wbsaboojsathi.gov.in, open the Bicycle Distribution or Distribution Record option. You then choose either a district wise or school wise view.
Select your district, then your block, then your school. The record shows how many cycles were allotted and distributed for that school.
If your school shows cycles distributed but you did not get one, that is a strong signal to raise a grievance, because the stock reached your school.
The record is public, so you do not need a password to use the district or school search. That makes it the easiest first check before you try logging in.
Note the allotment versus distributed figures shown for your school. A gap between the two means some cycles are still pending for that school, which is useful context for your own case.

extra_sections.title: Reading your distribution status
extra_sections.content:
If the record shows your school as pending, the cycles for your area have simply not arrived yet, and you wait for the batch.

If it shows distributed but you have nothing, the issue is local: either your name was missed on the list or collection was incomplete. That is a grievance case, not a waiting case.

extra_sections.heading: Common Login and Status Problems
content: A few issues trip students up when checking status. Most are easy to solve once you know them.
If the login rejects your details, check that the date of birth matches school records exactly. A mismatch there is the usual cause.
If the distribution search shows nothing, you may have picked the wrong block or school name. Reselect carefully, since schools with similar names are common.
If the portal is slow during peak distribution season, try again at a quieter time. Heavy traffic, not an error on your side, is often the reason.
If you still cannot resolve a login issue, the school office can confirm your Applicant ID and date of birth on record. That usually settles the mismatch quickly.

extra_sections.heading: How Students Actually Receive the Bicycle
content: The school prepares a list of eligible Class 9 to 12 students and sends it to the District Education Office. You do not fill any individual form.
Once the cycles for your area arrive, the school or block office announces a distribution date. Students collect the cycle in person.
An authorised officer of the block, municipality or sub-division formally hands over the bicycle. Keep any acknowledgement slip you are given.
Because supply is tied to tenders and batches, two schools in the same district may receive cycles at different times. A delay is not the same as rejection.
Distribution is usually held at the school or a nearby central point so students do not have to travel far to collect. Dates are announced through the school.
If you cannot attend on the announced day, speak to the school immediately. They can usually tell you how and when to collect your cycle afterwards.
On collection day, check the cycle before you leave the point. Confirm the brakes, tyres and seat are fine, because raising a fault on the spot is far easier than later.

extra_sections.title: One cycle, one student
extra_sections.content:
Saboojsathi gives one cycle per eligible student, once. It is not a yearly or repeatable benefit, so there is no annual renewal to chase.

What renews is eligibility for new students: every year a fresh batch of Class 9 students becomes eligible and is added by their schools.

extra_sections.heading: Why Saboojsathi Matters for Girls and Attendance
content: The scheme exists to fix one problem: the daily journey to school. For students living several kilometres away, that journey is the reason many stop attending.
Girls are affected most. Long or unsafe walks to school push many rural girls to drop out before finishing Class 12.
A free cycle changes the maths for a family. The child can reach school on her own, safely and on time, without depending on buses or paid transport.
This is why Saboojsathi is counted among West Bengal's most successful education schemes, with cycles given to crores of students over the years.
Studies of the scheme credit it with measurable gains in school retention. Fewer students, and fewer girls in particular, leave school between Class 9 and Class 12 where the cycle is available.
The supply chain behind it is large, involving bulk procurement and, in some phases, support from partners outside the state. That scale is what lets it reach crores of students.
For many families, the saving is real money. Without the cycle, a daily bus or van fare to a distant school adds up over a year and can tip a struggling family toward pulling the child out.

extra_sections.heading: The Role of the School in Saboojsathi
content: The school is the single most important link in this scheme. Everything from your eligibility to your cycle passes through it.
Teachers prepare the list of Class 9 to 12 students and send it to the District Education Office. A missing name almost always traces back to this list.
If you join a new school mid-year, tell the office you are eligible so you are added to the next list. Do not assume the transfer carries over automatically.
When in doubt about your status, the headmaster's office is faster than the portal, because they can see exactly whether your name was submitted.
Because the school controls the list, building a good relationship with the class teacher matters. They are the person who can confirm and fix your entry.
If the school says your name was submitted but the portal disagrees, ask them for the submission date or reference. That detail strengthens any grievance you raise.
Schools also handle re-issues to students who joined late or were missed. So even after the main distribution, a genuine eligible student can still be added in a later round.

extra_sections.title: Why some students are excluded
extra_sections.content:
The most common reason for missing out is studying in a private unaided school, which the scheme does not cover.

Other reasons are being outside the Class 9 to 12 range, or your name simply not being on the list the school submitted. If you qualify but are missing, the fix is to get your school to add you, then file a grievance if needed.

extra_sections.heading: How to File a Saboojsathi Grievance
content: If you are eligible but have not received a cycle, the portal has a grievance form at wbsaboojsathi.gov.in for exactly this.
Open the grievance page and choose whether you are a student or a member of the public. Then enter your name, current mobile number and the details of your complaint.
Describe the problem clearly, for example that your class received cycles but you were left out. You can attach a document if you have one, though it is not mandatory.
Submit the form and note any reference shown. Also tell your class teacher or headmaster, since the school controls the eligible list.
A strong grievance is specific. State your school, class, district and exactly what happened, rather than a vague complaint that you did not get a cycle.

extra_sections.heading: What to Keep and What to Carry
content: You do not need a stack of documents, because the school handles the paperwork. But a few things make your life easier.
Keep your Applicant ID safe once the school gives it. It is your key to logging in and checking status.
On the distribution day, carry a school identity proof so the officer can confirm you against the list. Collect any acknowledgement slip offered.
If you ever file a grievance, keep a note of the reference and the date. It helps when you follow up with the school or block office.
If you lose your Applicant ID, the school can retrieve it for you. It is tied to your enrolment, so it is recoverable rather than gone for good.
A small folder with your school ID, Applicant ID and any slip keeps everything in one place for the collection day and any follow-up.

extra_sections.heading: From List to Cycle in Hand
Why There Can Be a Delay
content: Saboojsathi serves lakhs of students across thousands of schools, so the cycles are bought and delivered in phases through a tender process.
This means your block may receive its batch weeks after a neighbouring block. The gap is about logistics, not about your eligibility.
Assembly and delivery of so many cycles takes a large supply chain. During peak distribution, thousands of cycles are prepared and moved every day.
So if your school is marked pending, the honest answer is usually patience. Check the record again in a few weeks before assuming a problem.
Track your status calmly over a few weeks rather than checking daily. The record updates as batches move, and a pending status often clears on its own.

If months pass and your school still shows nothing while neighbouring schools have received cycles, that is the point to escalate through the grievance route rather than keep waiting silently for the cycle to appear.

extra_sections.heading: How Saboojsathi Fits With Other Schemes
content: Saboojsathi rarely works alone in a student's life. It sits alongside other West Bengal schemes aimed at keeping children in school.
A girl in Class 9 to 12 may get the cycle through Saboojsathi and separate cash support through Kanyashree. The two are different schemes with different portals.
There are also scholarship schemes for higher studies and for minority students. Each has its own eligibility, but together they reduce the cost of staying in education.
The practical point is to claim every scheme you qualify for. Getting the cycle does not stop you from applying for cash and scholarship schemes too.
Keep a simple list of which schemes you have claimed and which you have not. It is easy to forget a scholarship deadline while focused on the cycle.

If you are unsure which schemes apply to you, our free eligibility checker can match your details against many central and state schemes at once. It takes under a minute and is the quickest way to spot benefits you are missing.

extra_sections.heading: Saboojsathi vs Other WB Student Help
Renewal, New Academic Year and Upgrades
content: The cycle is a one-time benefit per student under the scheme, not a yearly payment. Once you receive it, you are not in the queue again.
Each new academic year, fresh Class 9 students become eligible and are added by their schools. So younger siblings reaching Class 9 will get their own turn.
If your cycle has a fault at the time of handover, raise it immediately with the distributing officer rather than after you leave.
Keep the cycle and any paperwork safe. The scheme does not replace lost or damaged cycles, so the one handover is the benefit.
Families with daughters can also look at the Kanya Sumangala girl-child scheme.
Treat the cycle as a long-term asset. Maintaining it well means it can serve you right through to Class 12 and beyond.

extra_sections.text: Saboojsathi works because it removes one specific barrier: the daily journey to school. For a student several kilometres away, a cycle can be the difference between staying in school and dropping out.

faqs.question: How to check Saboojsathi status online in 2026?
faqs.answer:
Go to wbsaboojsathi.gov.in and use the Bicycle Distribution Record search, or log in with your Applicant ID and date of birth.

For the public search you enter your district, block, school and class to see the distribution status for your school.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Saboojsathi cycle?
faqs.answer:
Students of Class 9 to 12 in government, government-aided or government-sponsored schools and recognised madrasahs in West Bengal.

Private unaided school students and students outside Class 9 to 12 are not covered.

faqs.question: How do I log in to the Saboojsathi portal?
faqs.answer:
Open wbsaboojsathi.gov.in and use the student login with your Applicant ID and date of birth, which your school provides.

If you do not have an Applicant ID, use the public Bicycle Distribution Record search instead.

faqs.question: Do I need to apply for Saboojsathi myself?
faqs.answer:
No. There is no individual online application. Your school prepares a list of eligible students and sends it to the District Education Office.

Your task is to make sure your name is on that list and then track the distribution status.

faqs.question: What if I have not received my Saboojsathi cycle?
faqs.answer:
First confirm whether your school's batch has been distributed, since cycles arrive in batches at different times.

If your class got cycles but you were missed, file a grievance on the portal and inform your headmaster, who controls the list.

faqs.question: Is the Saboojsathi cycle really free?
faqs.answer:
Yes, it is fully free. The West Bengal government buys and distributes the cycles, and students pay nothing.

Anyone asking for a fee, deposit or agent charge is not genuine, so do not pay.

faqs.question: Can a private school student get a Saboojsathi cycle?
faqs.answer:
No. Only students in government, government-aided, government-sponsored schools and recognised madrasahs are eligible.

Students in private unaided schools are not covered by the scheme.

faqs.question: How many cycles has Saboojsathi distributed?
faqs.answer:
The scheme has distributed over 1.2 crore bicycles since it began in 2015.

It is one of West Bengal's largest student welfare schemes and is credited with improving school attendance, especially for girls.

faqs.question: Is the cycle given every year?
faqs.answer:
No. It is a one-time benefit per eligible student, not a yearly payment.

Each new academic year, fresh Class 9 students become eligible and are added by their schools.
